text:
maya: Quick heads-up — nightly regression for paged-flash-attn v2 on long sequences (seq=8192). memory bw up ~22%, smem stall time up, and end-to-end p95 latency +18%. attaching quick counters below. :eyes:
jin: ugh. landed which CL touched kernel selection?
alex: CL 4523 changed heuristic that prefers paged-flash for seq>4096 to reduce VRAM, might be hitting a perf cliff on Ampere64.
sienna: can you paste the perf counters?
maya: sure — short dump from perf-agent (readable):
```
ATTN_KERNEL=PagedFlashV2
seq=8192, batch=1
SMEM_STALLS=1.18e9 cycles
MEM_BANDWIDTH_BYTES=3.2e11
L2_READS=4.1e8
KV_CACHE_EVICTS=12 (per request)
warp_serialize_events=0.02%
end_to_end_p95_ms=312
baseline (fused-attn-v1): end_to_end_p95_ms=265
```
ryan: KV cache evicts per request of 12 is concerning for large seqs — could be prefetch/kv window misalignment causing extra loads.
jin: also saw the stall heatmap — majority of stalls during tile boundary sync when pipeline stage 2 -> 3 ramps up. might be tile_x too big for shared memory capacity under current SM occupancy.
alex: suggestion: try reducing tile_x from 256->192 or move to the alternative kernel path (fused-attn-pipelined) for seq>6144 as a temporary fallback.
sienna: how does batching heuristic play here? are we coalescing multiple small requests into a big batch that then triggers this kernel choice?
maya: for this run batch=1, but our batching heuristics later combine low-latency traffic into larger micro-batches when queue length > 20ms; that might explain customer-side behavior too.
perf-bot: auto-run: /bench/attn_longseq --kernel=paged_flash_v2 --seq=8192 --iter=50 -> p95=315ms, membw=3.21e11, smem_stalls=1.2e9
jin: OK repro is easy. alex, can you add an A/B in kernel router to prefer fused-attn-pipelined for 8192+ with a 10% rollout? if that fixes p95 we can rollback CL4523.
alex: will do. also will instrument a smem occupancy metric and KV eviction counter in runtime traces.
sienna: small note — quantized fused-attn (int8 kernels) had slightly worse accuracy on some evals, but maybe acceptable as a short-term perf mitigation; we should mark it in the rollout dashboard.
maya: timeline: alex to push router tweak + tracing by EOD, jin to run full batch sweep (seq 2048/4096/6144/8192) and share csv, ryan to check kv eviction window algo for off-by-one prefetching.
ryan: on it. I suspect the prefetch window is using MAX_KV_W=16 which with large seqs and page alignment causes thrash; will test W=8/12/16.
perf-bot: created perf issue #INFR-1127 and attached benchmark artifacts.
maya: thanks — if A/B shows improvement we can roll to 100% and revert the kernel preference change. :thumbsup:
jin: FYI added a small note to the changelog about this regression and the mitigation path.
alex: pushing canary now (will tag the rollout in console).
